data.name: Bran
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Celtic word ‘bran’, meaning ‘raven’ or ‘black one’. Bran was a popular name among ancient Celts and early Christians due to its association with bravery, strength, and the sacred raven. The name also symbolizes the wisdom of the raven, which was revered in Celtic mythology. Bran the Blessed is a legendary figure from Welsh folklore, often considered a patron saint of travelers and protectors of the dead.
data.spiritual_meaning: Emblem of divine protection and guidance

data.cultural_impact: The Celtic name "Bran" was popular among both the ancient Celts and early Christians due to its association with bravery, strength, and the sacred raven. The name's popularity persisted due to the enduring symbolism of the raven as a powerful and wise creature, often featured in mythology and folklore.
data.spiritual_significance: In Celtic mythology, the raven was considered a sacred creature, representing wisdom, protection, and the connection between the natural world and the spiritual realm. Bran the Blessed, a legendary Welsh figure, embodies the spiritual significance of the name as a patron saint of travelers and protectors of the dead, reinforcing the connection between the physical world and the afterlife.
